Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Copied action intents

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use net.Action_Intent(Action) to retain a UI or device action while submission is blocked and track its eventual authority result. It owns one copied, unsubmitted action and a bounded set of tickets already accepted by the network ledger; each ticket identifies one submitted request. It lives beside device/UI state, outside the simulation. It does not change action scheduling, admission, prediction, game predicates or checkpoint policy.

Odin
dash: net.Action_Intent(Action)

// Capture once when the game can construct the intended payload.
error := net.intent_capture(&dash, Action{kind=.Dash, aim=direction})

// Call each frame, including frames with no new press. A failed submission
// retains the payload; a successful one returns its sequence and consumes it.
sequence, error := inputgd.session_intent(&session, &dash)
// For a Room, use inputgd.room_intent(&room, &dash).

for change in changes {
    inputgd.intent_observe(&dash, &session, change)
}

// Menus or game policy may cancel input that has not yet been submitted.
net.intent_cancel(&dash)

Capture rejects reference-bearing payload types. Capturing while another payload is held returns Capacity and preserves the first value; this is a single intent latch, not an unlimited click queue. Submission also checks ticket capacity before calling the issuer. A successful issue owns delivery through the existing action ledger. Cancellation cannot withdraw that submitted action, and a predicate refusal completes its ticket without automatic retry.

The helper tracks tickets by epoch and sequence, because recovery can reuse a sequence number from a retired epoch. intent_observe accepts only authoritative action-result changes for the Session's local seat and a matching ticket. Predicted changes, cancellation, other seats, old epochs and duplicate results do not settle the ticket.

Session helpers process the existing recovery report. Retained requests move to the new epoch with their original sequence. Known applied/rejected results settle; retired requests and unavailable settled results increment distinct retired and unknown counters. Neither is treated as a gameplay rejection or blindly retried. Call the submit/observation helpers every frame and consume recovery reports in order; low-level users can call net.intent_recover explicitly.

submitted, confirmed, refused, retired, unknown, pending_count and captured are diagnostic state. last holds the most recently completed result; result_serial changes whenever one completes, including through recovery. A recovery batch can complete multiple tickets, so use the original Session changes and recovery report when every individual result is needed for application logic.

Use intent_reset only at an explicit local session lifecycle boundary, before reusing the helper with another ledger. It does not cancel work in a running network session. One helper must not mix results from unrelated sessions.

Low-level client_intent and server_intent use the same mechanism. Custom intent_submit callbacks must enqueue once, return a nonzero increasing sequence for the supplied epoch, and avoid reentry or synchronous resolution. A broken success receipt faults the helper to prevent automatic duplicate submission; the helper cannot undo an external callback's side effects.
